name: What is R-value in insulation?

acceptedAnswer.text: R-value is a measure of thermal resistance, indicating how well an insulation material resists the conductive flow of heat. A higher R-value means greater insulating power. The ideal R-value for your home depends on your climate zone, the specific area being insulated (e.g., attic, walls, floor), and the insulation material. Local building codes also specify minimum R-values for different parts of a home.
acceptedAnswer.description: R-value measures insulation's resistance to heat flow; a higher number means better insulation. Required R-values vary by climate and location.
